summary: Iter 389 - Backend + Frontend E2E for the new Video Consultation REPORT + HISTORY feature. Backend: 5/5 pytest pass on /sessions/{id}/end (email_sent=true), /sessions/{id}/report.pdf (200, application/pdf, %PDF magic, attachment), 404 for non-owner, 404 unknown id, and /sessions list. Frontend E2E (mobile 390x844, famtester wallet=353 EUR): login -> /video-consult -> Historique opens empty/list -> reserve vp_doc1 15min -> Lobby (37,50 EUR) -> Démarrer l'appel -> Jitsi iframe (sbconsult-<token>) -> Quitter -> 'Consultation terminée !' (video-consult-success) WITH 'Compte-rendu PDF envoyé par e-mail' (report-email-note) AND download-report-btn that downloads a real 2535-byte PDF (%PDF). Re-opening Historique now lists the just-completed session (history-vsess_*) with per-line PDF download (also returns a valid PDF). back-from-history returns to provider list. All 5 backend test cases + every UI step PASS.
critical_code_review_comments: end_video_session: PDF generation and email fire are wrapped in a bare 'except Exception: pass' (gojek_services.py line 149). If PDF/email ever fails, the user still sees email_sent=true ONLY when the try block reaches the fire() call; however a silent generic except still masks real errors (e.g., reportlab import failure, malformed session). Recommend logging at WARNING with the traceback so prod regressions surface in logs.

end_video_session returns email_sent=true based purely on the fact that fire() was invoked, not on actual Resend success. Acceptable because Resend is fire-and-forget; document this in the API spec so the frontend message 'envoyé par e-mail' is honest about the asynchronous nature.

download_consultation_report regenerates the PDF on every GET (no caching). Fine at 2.5KB, but if reportlab cost grows or attachments are added, cache the bytes in the session document or in object storage.

list_video_sessions has no pagination cap beyond .to_list(50). Hardcoded magic number; once a power user accumulates >50 consults the 'Mes consultations' history silently truncates. Move 50 to a constant and add a TODO for pagination.

consult_pdf.consultation_report_pdf is invoked twice for the same session (once in end_video_session to email, once in download_consultation_report on click). Minor duplication; consider extracting a memoised helper if PDF generation becomes heavier.

VideoConsultPage.handleEndCall swallows fetch errors silently (catch (e) {}). If /end fails (e.g., 500), the user still lands on the success screen without ever seeing email_sent=true. Consider surfacing a discreet toast on failure.

openHistory() in VideoConsultPage filters status==='completed' client-side. The list endpoint returns up to 50 sessions of any status, so this is fine for now but couples the FE to a BE contract; an API query param (?status=completed) would be cleaner.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (full E2E: book -> join -> Jitsi mount -> Quitter -> success screen with report-email-note + PDF download + history listing with per-line PDF download)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression: re-run /app/backend/tests/test_iter389_consult_report.py (safe so long as famtester wallet stays >= ~75 EUR). The history endpoint /api/video-consult/sessions returns ALL statuses; the FE filters status=='completed'. Resend is in test mode so real emails only reach the verified owner address — DO NOT assert on inbox, only assert email_sent=true is returned. Jitsi gum.not_found errors in headless are expected and harmless. The Quitter button (data-testid=video-call-leave) sometimes needs a JS .click() dispatch via page.evaluate when the iframe steals pointer events; a normal force=True playwright click may visually fail but the fallback works reliably.
rca of the issue: No bug found. Initial UI test attempt had a transient click-through issue on the 'Quitter' button (data-testid=video-call-leave) because the Jitsi iframe occasionally captures pointer events on first paint. Re-running with a JS-dispatched .click() in page.evaluate() resolved it instantly — the underlying React handler (handleEndCall) ran exactly as designed: POST /end -> setBooked({...emailSent:true}) -> success screen with report-email-note + download-report-btn -> PDF served by GET /report.pdf (2535 bytes, %PDF). History endpoint returns the freshly-completed session and each line correctly streams its own PDF. No code changes needed.
